findings.title: Deferred cancellation leaves a gap in which cancelled emails are still sent
findings.body: The default path only sets `cancelled = true` in the DB. The cron job cancels at most one hour ahead and runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before the reminder's send time, the next cron run may fire after the send time, or the reminder may only enter the 1-hour window after the last run. The row is then deleted by the 'scheduledDate <= now' cleanup and the SendGrid email goes out anyway. When `scheduledDate` is already within the next hour, the code should cancel in SendGrid right away instead of waiting for the cron.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel blocks all remaining cancellations and the DB deletes
findings.body: The loop awaits `client.request` for each reminder inside a single try/catch. If one request throws (for example an invalid or already-sent batch id, or a 4xx), the loop exits. Reminders later in the list are not cancelled in that run. The Prisma `delete` calls collected so far are lazy and are never awaited, so nothing is deleted either. That failing reminder stays `cancelled: true` and is retried first on every run until its `scheduledDate` passes. A permanently failing entry can therefore keep the other cancelled emails from being cancelled, so they get sent. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete each row right after its cancel succeeds.

findings.title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancel, bringing back the 100-pending-cancellation limit
findings.body: On reschedule, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` posts a SendGrid cancel immediately. That is the same path the PR says fails once about 100 cancellations are pending, so emails are still sent. This is inconsistent with `requestReschedule` and `handleCancelBooking`, which use the deferred path. The workflow-delete and step-delete paths also pass `true`; they need it because the DB rows are cascade-deleted. After an immediate cancel nothing is recorded on the row. If SendGrid rejects the cancel, the row is not marked `cancelled` and the cron will not retry, so the email is sent. On failure, fall back to marking the row `cancelled: true`.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now do the DB writes (set `cancelled` or delete the row) and call Twilio, but they are fire-and-forget. The old code awaited the Prisma deletes via `Promise.all`. In a serverless runtime the invocation can end before the update runs, leaving the reminder uncancelled and the email still sent. The same applies to the loop in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule`. Collect these promises and await them, for example in the existing `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import, and type imports changed to value imports
findings.body: `Prisma` is now imported as a value but no longer used, since the `deleteReminderPromise` code was removed, which will fail lint. `PrismaPromise` and `Prisma` were `import type` before and are now regular imports. The same change was made to `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` in `handleNewBooking.ts`. Regular imports of type-only symbols can break under `isolatedModules`/SWC. The line also lacks a trailing comma. The diff also re-indents the commented-out `testAction` block, which is unrelated noise.
